paper.title: Online Improper Learning with an Approximation Oracle

unmapped: Player plays in K but competes with best point in a (possibly different) target set K*; access only via an improper linear optimization oracle O_{K,K*} returning a point of K at least as good as the best of K* in directions of a cone W
Loss vectors lie in a convex cone W intersected with B(0,L)
The learner knows the loss norm bound L
settings.definition_quote: In round $t$, the player chooses a point $x_t \in \K$ while an adversary chooses a loss vector $f_t \in W \cap B(0, L)$ ($L>0$), and then the player incurs a loss $f_t^\top x_t$. ... $\Reg_{\K, \K^*}(T) := \sum_{t=1}^T f_t^\top x_t - \min_{x^* \in \K^*} \sum_{t=1}^T f_t^\top x^*$.

settings.name_in_paper: alpha-regret minimization with an approximation oracle (full information)
unmapped: Access only through an alpha-approximate linear optimization oracle over K
Non-negative loss vectors (W subset of R_+^d) with norm at most L; K subset of R_+^d
The learner knows the loss norm bound L
settings.definition_quote: the player has access to an approximate linear optimization oracle $\O_\K^\alpha$ over $\K$ ($\alpha>1$) ... $\Reg^\alpha_\K(T) := \sum_{t=1}^T f_t^\top x_t - \alpha \min_{x \in \K} \sum_{t=1}^T f_t^\top x$.

settings.name_in_paper: alpha-regret minimization in the bandit setting
unmapped: Access through an alpha-approximate linear optimization oracle over K plus a known beta-barycentric spanner of K
Non-negative loss vectors (W = R_+^d) with norm at most L; K subset of R_+^d cap B(0,R)
The learner knows the loss norm bound L and the spanner constant beta
settings.definition_quote: In this section we consider the $\alpha$-regret minimization problem in the bandit setting, where $W = \reals_+^d$, $\K \subseteq \reals_+^d \cap B(0, R)$ and $\K^* = \alpha \K$. Similar to \citep{kakade2009playing}, we assume we know a \emph{$\beta$-barycentric spanner} for $\K$.

source.quote: Suppose $(\varphi,W)$ satisfies the PNIP property. Then for any $\epsilon, \eta>0$, Algorithm 1 satisfies ... In particular, if $\varphi$ is $\mu$-strongly convex and $A \ge \max_{x^* \in \K^*} (\varphi(x^*)-\varphi(y_1))$, setting $\epsilon = \frac{R}{T}$ and $\eta = \frac1L\sqrt{\frac{2\mu A}{T}}$, we have $\forall x^* \in \K^*: \E[\sum_t ( f_t(\tilde x_t)-f_t(x^*) )] \le L\sqrt{\frac{2AT }{\mu}}+LR.$
